deploy_diversify|diversified_global.fence: A low fence: manage concentration by diversifying supply, not by restricting it.
deploy_diversify|diversified_global.gate: Wide open, and widened: trade agreements and procurement that reward supplier diversity bring in more producers. Delivery (diversified global): The gate stays wide open to a broad supplier base.
deploy_diversify|diversified_global.build: Build what enables deployment and diversify supply toward trusted producers, not a domestic replica. Delivery (diversified global): Supply comes from a diversified global base; the build is enabling infrastructure, not production.
deploy_diversify|diversified_global.benchmark: The largest potentially coercive supplier's share of the country's supply falls below the watch line without a material rise in delivered cost.
deploy_diversify|diversified_global.exit: Returns to deploy when supply is diversified below the watch lines. Re-test for Secure if the coercive supplier's share passes the screening line and the substitution and timing legs hold, or if a control layer is identified.

deploy|diversified_global.fence: A low fence: cross-cutting safeguards only (genuine trade remedies, forced-labour restrictions, basic security and safety standards).
deploy|diversified_global.gate: Wide open: diversified imports, broad supplier access and competition keep the good cheap and fast to deploy. Delivery (diversified global): The gate stays wide open to a broad supplier base.
deploy|diversified_global.build: Build what enables deployment (infrastructure, permitting, interoperability, procurement efficiency, supply-chain transparency), not domestic production. Delivery (diversified global): Supply comes from a diversified global base; the build is enabling infrastructure, not production.
deploy|diversified_global.benchmark: Delivered cost and deployment pace match or beat peers, with diversified supply and adequate resilience. Domestic production share is not a benchmark.
deploy|diversified_global.exit: Re-test if concentration rises (the largest coercive supplier or the import HHI crosses its watch line), a control layer or physical chokepoint is identified, or a credible capability case emerges.

deploy_diversify|allied.fence: A low fence: manage concentration by diversifying supply, not by restricting it.
deploy_diversify|allied.gate: Wide open, and widened: trade agreements and procurement that reward supplier diversity bring in more producers. Delivery (allied): The gate stays wide open; allied sourcing is a diversification tool, not an exclusion of other lawful suppliers.
deploy_diversify|allied.build: Build what enables deployment and diversify supply toward trusted producers, not a domestic replica. Delivery (allied): Diversify toward trusted partners through offtake and standards recognition, not production subsidies.
deploy_diversify|allied.benchmark: The largest potentially coercive supplier's share of the country's supply falls below the watch line without a material rise in delivered cost.
deploy_diversify|allied.exit: Returns to deploy when supply is diversified below the watch lines. Re-test for Secure if the coercive supplier's share passes the screening line and the substitution and timing legs hold, or if a control layer is identified.

secure_resilience|allied.fence: No fence: the risk is the loss of an essential supply that takes years to rebuild, not a coercive actor. Restricting imports would deepen the shortfall it guards against.
secure_resilience|allied.gate: Selective: open to allied and other trusted supply, investment and equipment that add capacity or shorten the time to rebuild; screening only of foreign control of the essential assets themselves. Delivery (allied): The gate stays open to those partners' products, investment and equipment, and trusted-source rules recognise allied suppliers.
secure_resilience|allied.build: Build resilience rather than replacement: reserves and stockpiles sized to the rebuild time, long-lead procurement frameworks, spares and redundancy, demand-side flexibility, and capacity agreements with trusted partners. Delivery (allied): Build trusted capacity with partners, not at home: compacts, offtake agreements, co-investment and shared stockpiles with allied producers.
secure_resilience|allied.benchmark: The essential function could continue on reserves and trusted supply for longer than it takes to rebuild supply.
secure_resilience|allied.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when reserves and trusted alternatives cover the rebuild time, or the country's import dependence falls below the line.

compete_partner|allied.fence: A low fence: the capability is met with trusted partners, so the home market stays open to them; cross-cutting safeguards only.
compete_partner|allied.gate: Open to the recommended trusted partners' products, investment and technology; partnership terms, not tariffs, decide who supplies. Delivery (allied): The gate stays open to the partners' investment, equipment and engineers, with conditions that favour capability transfer.
compete_partner|allied.build: Build the partnership, not a domestic replica: offtake and co-investment with the recommended partners, diversified contracts and the infrastructure that brings partner supply in. Delivery (allied): Build the capability jointly with partners (co-investment, joint ventures, offtake, shared R&D); the domestic share is the segment where the country is strongest.
compete_partner|allied.benchmark: Trusted partners supply the bulk of the country's need at a delivered cost close to the world price.
compete_partner|allied.exit: Public finance for partner capacity sunsets on the stated schedule unless partner supply is growing. Re-test when the country's opportunity in the node rises (Catch Up or Preserve), its need falls (Watch), or a partner gap opens (no credible trusted supplier).

compete_partner|diversified_global.fence: A low fence: the capability is met with trusted partners, so the home market stays open to them; cross-cutting safeguards only.
compete_partner|diversified_global.gate: Open to the recommended trusted partners' products, investment and technology; partnership terms, not tariffs, decide who supplies. Delivery (diversified global): The gate stays wide for inputs and equipment from a diversified global base.
compete_partner|diversified_global.build: Build the partnership, not a domestic replica: offtake and co-investment with the recommended partners, diversified contracts and the infrastructure that brings partner supply in. Delivery (diversified global): Build a specialised niche in global value chains, the segment where the country is strongest, and source the rest competitively.
compete_partner|diversified_global.benchmark: Trusted partners supply the bulk of the country's need at a delivered cost close to the world price.
compete_partner|diversified_global.exit: Public finance for partner capacity sunsets on the stated schedule unless partner supply is growing. Re-test when the country's opportunity in the node rises (Catch Up or Preserve), its need falls (Watch), or a partner gap opens (no credible trusted supplier).

secure_resilience|mixed.fence: No fence: the risk is the loss of an essential supply that takes years to rebuild, not a coercive actor. Restricting imports would deepen the shortfall it guards against.
secure_resilience|mixed.gate: Selective: open to allied and other trusted supply, investment and equipment that add capacity or shorten the time to rebuild; screening only of foreign control of the essential assets themselves. Delivery (mixed): The gate stays open to allied partners' technology, equipment and investment for the capacity not built at home.
secure_resilience|mixed.build: Build resilience rather than replacement: reserves and stockpiles sized to the rebuild time, long-lead procurement frameworks, spares and redundancy, demand-side flexibility, and capacity agreements with trusted partners. Delivery (mixed): No source holds enough trusted supply to repair the vulnerability alone: create new trusted capacity at home (where a foothold exists or can be built) and with allied partners through co-investment and offtake, and bridge the years until it qualifies with stockpiles.
secure_resilience|mixed.benchmark: The essential function could continue on reserves and trusted supply for longer than it takes to rebuild supply.
secure_resilience|mixed.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when reserves and trusted alternatives cover the rebuild time, or the country's import dependence falls below the line.

deploy_floor|diversified_global.fence: A low fence with a limited, specified domestic capability floor whose premium is stated.
deploy_floor|diversified_global.gate: Wide open for the rest of demand: diversified imports, broad supplier access and competition. Delivery (diversified global): The gate stays wide open to a broad supplier base.
deploy_floor|diversified_global.build: Keep a specified capability floor (what it preserves, how much is enough, the premium, the review date) and otherwise build what enables deployment. Delivery (diversified global): Supply comes from a diversified global base; the build is enabling infrastructure, not production.
deploy_floor|diversified_global.benchmark: The floor preserves the capability it was specified to preserve at no more than the stated premium, while deployment stays cheap and fast.
deploy_floor|diversified_global.exit: Reduce or remove the floor at review if it is not preserving the capability or its premium rises. Re-test if concentration rises or a control layer is identified, and return to Compete only if the capability case becomes strong.

compete_preserve|domestic.fence: Calibrated, temporary protection only where unfair competition threatens an established base.
compete_preserve|domestic.gate: Open with conditions: allied and conditional investment, equipment imports, talent and import competition keep the industry at the frontier. Delivery (domestic): The gate stays open to foreign technology, capital and talent on terms that deepen domestic capability.
compete_preserve|domestic.build: Keep the established position competitive: process and next-generation R&D, workforce and supplier development, and finance for expansion, tied to benchmarks. Delivery (domestic): Build at home: production support, finance, workforce and supplier development for the domestic industry, tied to benchmarks.
compete_preserve|domestic.benchmark: Yields, cost and quality stay at the global frontier while public support per unit falls.
compete_preserve|domestic.exit: Support sunsets at each review unless the benchmarks are met. Move to Deploy if the capability case fails, and re-test for Secure if a control layer or coercive chokepoint is identified.

compete_catch_up|domestic.fence: Calibrated, temporary protection for the learning base, with the gate left open to the frontier.
compete_catch_up|domestic.gate: Open: licensing and joint ventures on terms that transfer capability. Learning from the frontier is the point of catching up. Delivery (domestic): The gate stays open to foreign technology, capital and talent on terms that deepen domestic capability.
compete_catch_up|domestic.build: Close the gap to the frontier: time-limited production incentives, first-of-a-kind finance, workforce and supplier development and demand creation, all tied to benchmarks. Delivery (domestic): Build at home: production support, finance, workforce and supplier development for the domestic industry, tied to benchmarks.
compete_catch_up|domestic.benchmark: The cost and quality gap to the frontier narrows on a stated schedule while support per unit falls.
compete_catch_up|domestic.exit: Support sunsets on the stated schedule unless the gap is narrowing. Move to Deploy if benchmarks are missed at successive reviews or the capability case fails, and re-test for Secure if a control layer or coercive chokepoint is identified.

secure_input|mixed.fence: A targeted fence that limits a coercive supplier's leverage over the input, without cutting supply before trusted alternatives qualify.
secure_input|mixed.gate: Selective: open to allied and other trusted producers, their investment and equipment, and to alternative inputs; the coercive supplier's share falls as trusted supply qualifies. Delivery (mixed): The gate stays open to allied partners' technology, equipment and investment for the capacity not built at home.
secure_input|mixed.build: Repair the chokepoint until a prolonged cutoff could be survived: qualified trusted supply (domestic or allied), stockpiles, surge and redundancy. The goal is mitigation, not maximum localisation. Delivery (mixed): No source holds enough trusted supply to repair the vulnerability alone: create new trusted capacity at home (where a foothold exists or can be built) and with allied partners through co-investment and offtake, and bridge the years until it qualifies with stockpiles.
secure_input|mixed.benchmark: Critical production could continue through a prolonged cutoff on inventories plus qualified trusted supply.
secure_input|mixed.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when a prolonged cutoff could be survived (trusted supply, stockpiles and surge cover the restore time) or the largest coercive supplier falls below the screening line. Announced capacity does not count until it is qualified.

secure_resilience|diversified_global.fence: No fence: the risk is the loss of an essential supply that takes years to rebuild, not a coercive actor. Restricting imports would deepen the shortfall it guards against.
secure_resilience|diversified_global.gate: Selective: open to allied and other trusted supply, investment and equipment that add capacity or shorten the time to rebuild; screening only of foreign control of the essential assets themselves. Delivery (diversified global): The gate stays open to every trusted producer; the restriction applies only to the coercive supplier on the fenced node.
secure_resilience|diversified_global.build: Build resilience rather than replacement: reserves and stockpiles sized to the rebuild time, long-lead procurement frameworks, spares and redundancy, demand-side flexibility, and capacity agreements with trusted partners. Delivery (diversified global): Repair the vulnerability by qualifying several trusted suppliers abroad and holding stockpiles, not by building a domestic replica.
secure_resilience|diversified_global.benchmark: The essential function could continue on reserves and trusted supply for longer than it takes to rebuild supply.
secure_resilience|diversified_global.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when reserves and trusted alternatives cover the rebuild time, or the country's import dependence falls below the line.

secure_dual_use|allied.fence: A high fence around the national-security end uses (defence and critical infrastructure), not around the whole market: those uses take only trusted supply.
secure_dual_use|allied.gate: Selective: allied producers and their investment qualify for the restricted end uses; the rest of the market stays open. Delivery (allied): The gate stays open to those partners' products, investment and equipment, and trusted-source rules recognise allied suppliers.
secure_dual_use|allied.build: Build enough trusted capacity, at home or with allies, to supply the national-security end uses through a cutoff; the civilian market is served openly. Delivery (allied): Build trusted capacity with partners, not at home: compacts, offtake agreements, co-investment and shared stockpiles with allied producers.
secure_dual_use|allied.benchmark: The national-security end uses could be supplied through a prolonged cutoff from trusted sources alone.
secure_dual_use|allied.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when trusted supply covers the restricted end uses through a cutoff, or the coercive suppliers' share of the country's supply falls below the screening line.

compete_catch_up|mixed.fence: Calibrated, temporary protection for the learning base, with the gate left open to the frontier.
compete_catch_up|mixed.gate: Open: licensing and joint ventures on terms that transfer capability. Learning from the frontier is the point of catching up. Delivery (mixed): The gate stays open to allied partners' investment and equipment, with conditions that favour capability transfer.
compete_catch_up|mixed.build: Close the gap to the frontier: time-limited production incentives, first-of-a-kind finance, workforce and supplier development and demand creation, all tied to benchmarks. Delivery (mixed): Build at home where the base is established and with allied partners for the rest, through co-investment and offtake.
compete_catch_up|mixed.benchmark: The cost and quality gap to the frontier narrows on a stated schedule while support per unit falls.
compete_catch_up|mixed.exit: Support sunsets on the stated schedule unless the gap is narrowing. Move to Deploy if benchmarks are missed at successive reviews or the capability case fails, and re-test for Secure if a control layer or coercive chokepoint is identified.

secure_input|allied.gate: Selective: open to allied and other trusted producers, their investment and equipment, and to alternative inputs; the coercive supplier's share falls as trusted supply qualifies. Delivery (allied): The gate stays open to those partners' products, investment and equipment, and trusted-source rules recognise allied suppliers.
secure_input|allied.build: Repair the chokepoint until a prolonged cutoff could be survived: qualified trusted supply (domestic or allied), stockpiles, surge and redundancy. The goal is mitigation, not maximum localisation. Delivery (allied): Build trusted capacity with partners, not at home: compacts, offtake agreements, co-investment and shared stockpiles with allied producers.
secure_input|allied.benchmark: Critical production could continue through a prolonged cutoff on inventories plus qualified trusted supply.
secure_input|allied.exit: Reclassify to Compete or Deploy when a prolonged cutoff could be survived (trusted supply, stockpiles and surge cover the restore time) or the largest coercive supplier falls below the screening line. Announced capacity does not count until it is qualified.
